newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Malaysian firm to build power plant in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian firm to build power plant in Cambodia.

text.p: Malaysia-based Global Technological Support Sdn Bhd has signed a $28 million contract to build a power plant in the eastern Cambodian town of Kompong Cham, officials said.

The 25-year, independent power producer contract provides for the upgrade of an existing 2.2 megawatt plant by mid-1997 and the construction of a new, 20-megawatt facility two years later, a Ministry of Industry, Mines and Energy statement said.

"The project demonstrates the commitment and involvement of the...government in solving the shortage of electricity in the nation," said Industry Minister Pou Southirak at a signing ceremony on Thursday night.
Cambodia's power infrastructure is dilapidated after decades of civil war, and the government has been working to rehabilitate electricity plants in its major cities and provincial towns.

Second Prime Minister Hun Sen said at Thursday's signing the four provinces of Kompong Cham, coastal Kompong Som, and Battambang and Siem Reap in the northwest were the top priorities. The project in the town of Kompong Cham, about 75 kilometres (47 miles) northeast of Phnom Penh, is the government's third independent power producer agreement.
